articles.title: Iraq Refuses to Accept OPEC+ Assessment of its Production Capacity
articles.description: Iraq is refusing to accept an OPEC+ assessment that says the country can sustainably produce less than 5 million barrels of oil per day. Baghdad wants OPEC+ to recognize a capacity of around 6 million bpd—an important acknowledgment ahead of the group’s upcoming Sunday meeting, at which production targets for 2027 are expected to be a topic of discussion. articles.title: Canada’s Oilfield Services Sector Is Gearing Up for a Stronger 2027
articles.description: Canada’s oilfield services market is ending 2026 stronger than it began. Well spuds fell 3%, and the number of fracked wells fell 5% in the first half, but a sharp second-half pickup, driven by higher commodity prices after the US-Iran war, leaves drilling and completion activity flat for the year measured by total wells spud and wells fracked. articles.description: Equinor has agreed to supply German energy company VNG with natural gas for 18 years, with deliveries beginning on 1 January 2027 and running until the end of 2044.

articles.description: Europe’s gas prices surged to four-year highs in October, with the TTF benchmark futures rising by 12% from the previous month and soaring by 163% from October 2025, amid tightening market balances ahead of the heating season, the latest monthly report by the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) showed on Tuesday. “Looking ahead, prolonged supply constraints, combined with colder-than-normal weather, could further tighten market balances and expose prices to upward pressure,” GECF said in the report. articles.title: Saudi Arabia Sees Smaller Economic Slump as More Oil Reaches Market
articles.description: Saudi Arabia now expects its economy to shrink 2.1% this year instead of 3.6%, after recovering enough oil exports to mitigate some of the damage caused by the Iran war. The revised forecast, announced in Tuesday's budget statement, is a considerable improvement from last month, but before the war began, Saudi Arabia had been expecting economic growth of approximately 4.5%. articles.title: EU to Seek Overhaul of UN Climate Consensus Decisions After COP31 Failure
articles.description: The European Union will propose to the UN to review the consensus decision-making model of the COP climate conferences after the latest summit ended without a deal but with a lot of quarrels about whether the final communique should include fossil fuels. After two days of overtime and tense negotiations, the COP31 in Antalya ended early on Sunday without a climate deal, for the first time since 2009, as countries failed to agree on fossil fuel commitments and climate financing. articles.title: Iran Faces a Deepening Natural Gas Crisis Ahead of Winter
articles.description: Iran is heading into winter facing a worsening natural gas shortage, as damage to key processing facilities during the war with the United States and Israel compounds years of chronic supply deficits. President Masud Pezeshkian warned on November 21 that the country would likely face energy supply problems this winter. "Even before this, we were facing an energy imbalance, and now attacks on the country's gas infrastructure have made this imbalance worse. We expect to face problems in the winter," Pezeshkian said. articles.title: Iraq Seeks Federal Control Over Disputed Kurdistan Oilfields
articles.description: The Iraqi government wants oilfields in the semi-autonomous Kurdistan region owned by the federally-held North Oil Company to be placed under federal control after uncovering oil smuggling in the northern fields, Iraq’s Oil Minister, Basim Mohammed Khudair, has said. “An investigation has been conducted, the findings of which will yield specific recommendations. articles.title: South Korea Says Its Crude Supply Is Stable Through the Winter
articles.description: South Korea has secured crude oil supplies for November and December, at 90% of last year’s levels, despite the Middle East crisis and the disruption to trade flows at the Strait of Hormuz, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources of one of Asia’s top crude importers said on Tuesday. South Korea has also procured supply for January, with current deals for January delivery accounting for 75% of the previous year’s levels, the authorities said. articles.title: European Gas Prices Climb as Cold Snap Threatens Depleted Reserves
articles.description: European benchmark natural gas prices rose on Tuesday for the fourth consecutive trading session as a cold snap this week is set to accelerate withdrawals from storage, where levels were at multi-year lows at the start of the heating season. The front-month price at the Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF), the benchmark for Europe’s gas trading, topped $98.77 (90.50 euros) per megawatt-hour (MWh) in the early morning in Amsterdam trade, rising by about 1% and extending the sharp gains from Monday. articles.title: Japan Poised to Ramp Up LNG Buying as Power Prices Surge
articles.description: Japanese utilities may raise spot LNG cargo buying as surging electricity prices in recent days have made gas-fired power generation profitable for the first time since the Iran war began. Japan’s physical spark spread, the difference between the price received by a power-generating facility for electricity produced, has turned positive on a seven-day average for the first time since the Middle East conflict began, data compiled by Bloomberg showed on Tuesday. articles.title: Equinor Locks In Longest Gas Supply Deal in 40 Years
articles.description: Equinor has signed an 18-year gas supply agreement with Germany’s energy firm VNG in the longest gas sales agreement the Norwegian energy major has signed since 1986. Under the deal with VNG, announced on Tuesday, Equinor will supply up to 15.3 TWh, or around 1.4 billion cubic meters (bcm), of natural gas per year to VNG, starting on January 1, 2027.
